I really wanted to give this restaurant a higher rating because there were some great positives. The food itself was good, and I liked that we could choose the portion size, the type of fish, and how it was cooked—it made the experience feel quite personalised.
Unfortunately, the visit was let down by a strong unpleasant smell of cat urine, which was noticeable throughout. We did mention it to the staff, and while they placed a scented candle nearby, it didn’t resolve the issue. The owner didn’t seem particularly concerned either, which was disappointing.
It’s a shame because the location is fantastic, and the food had potential, but the smell completely spoiled the experience for us. For that reason, I wouldn’t recommend it.

reviews.title: Not quite London or Indian standard but acceptable given in Egypt. Interesting decor. Fans too harsh so turn off! Okvfm
reviews.text:
12/12/23 Tuesday evening dinner

We three middle aged guys from London were after a bit of spice for our evening meal. Two of us had been here in January and liked the authenticity. We know a lot of Indian Restaurants in London and this was comparably good last January according to them.

We arrived at 19:45 after getting E£1000 cash out of the Bank of Cairo free ATM by the New Yalla Hotel near the similarly named (Nirv..) beachside restaurant.

This restaurant was a fairly large room that must have been a takeaway space then an extension over the pavement years ago. We took a table by the wall of ephemera, none particularly religious. 

The friendly waiter presented us with a menu each which had a reasonable choice of the standard Indian fare. 

We ordered at about 20:10hrs specifically asking for our main dishes to be hot (we live in London).

We ordered:
Raita 50
Garlic Naan 30
Peshwari Naan 50
Vegetable Biryani 75
Paneer Makhani 165
Dahl Makhani 90
Malai Kofta 125
Fish Tikka Marsala 250
(Total 835)

The food started arriving at 20:30. It was in standard portions (mostly in korai - stainless steel bowls but not huge as some reviewers have said).

A small bowl of sliced pickled onions (red as probably infused with beetroot) was good as they were crisp and spicy. 

A small bowl of spicy oil was provided which it turned out to be the extra 'spice' for the dishes. Not the London style!

The naans were also not huge (as some have said) probably because of the inflation in Egypt and the peshwari naan was not as stuffed as it could have been (sorry we are from London where they can be well stuffed!). 

The paneer makhani was well liked by my friend. He found it very tasty and quite spicy but not spicy enough.

The dahl makhani was also tasty albeit on the small side. Cumin was the main taste.

The malai kofta were four very stodgy potatoey balls in a thick indeterminate curry sauce - nothing special. They are actually quite rare on menus in London and these were unlike any of them we have encountered (we've also travelled in South India/Tamil Nadu but not the North where this cuisine is probably from).

My fish tikka marsala curry was either tilapia or bassa (the fish was not specified and I did not ask).  It was a fair amount but was very earthy with almost a bleach undertone. There were no bones though thankfully but I found it quite hard work to finish as I resolve never to leave food on my plate ever! The fish should be specified and hopefully locally sourced as this was technically a fishing village in the past although local fishing is rightly forbidden around the reef for obvious reasons. The market and mainstream fish restaurants on the beach had fresh bright eyed fish on their icy display stands.

We finished our dishes and I managed to finish what was left, finishing with the cool raita (reasonable size but expensive for what it was). I was actually very full but the spices can make you feel this way despite the volume. 

During our stay there were various other diners, mostly North Americans. The place was not busy at all but it was off tourism peak and a Tuesday. 

By 21:05 we had finished and it took a while to get the waiter's attention to order the bill. I think they were happy we were there to attract more people in. 

The printed bill arrived at and was an accurate 835.

As we had brought our own cans of beer we were happy and passed over 900 in total including the tip.

We left very full (I was quite bloated but I had finished off all the leftovers). My friends are happy that they had returned after eleven months and had a good Indian meal. I had my reservations though. We had not tried the central beach front competition (...vana) so could not compare it although our edge of busy town choice would have been a lot cheaper!

When we arrived all the fans were on full blast and it was actually quite cold under them. We asked for ours to be turned off which the waiter did and we were much more comfortable. 

Nobody else was smoking inside whilst we were there.

The service was painfully slow; we waited over an hour for our food, and my children literally fell asleep at the table while waiting. When the food finally arrived, it was far from authentic Italian, despite their claims. The hype surrounding this place is completely unjustified. Dahab has plenty of Italian restaurants—do yourself a favor and choose any other one. This was my first and absolutely my last visit.

reviews.title: BEST ITALIAN RESTAURANT IN EGYPT...AND MORE!
reviews.text: Dai Pescatori in Dahab is an oasis of peace outside the center, on the seafront, and is not only *absolutely* the best restaurant in the entire Egyptian nation, but for some dishes it is an even better table than many restaurants in Italy. Whether you are looking for pasta cooked perfectly al dente, a raw grouper carpaccio, linguine with lobster, Recco focaccia, gnocchi with pesto or Sorrento, a fresh buffalo mozzarella (otherwise not found in Sinai) or a tender fillet with green pepper, this corner of paradise with an informal climate, pieds-dans-l'eaux, on a microscopic beach in Dahab with tables on the sand, is an unmissable appointment, it is not comparable to any other restaurant that is in Dahab or Sharm, so much so that we went there for dinner every night during our stay. Owner Nader, a man of exceptional elegance and intelligence who lived several decades in Italy before returning to Egypt, has now opened a branch in Cairo, which is having great success. Good luck to the Fishermen, and good appetite to all!

reviews.title: Extremely over hyped, very bad
reviews.text:
We heard all about Dai Pescatori from friends in Dahab so we decided to give it a go. We went to have dinner on Sunday July 2nd 2023. We had Dai Pescatori Salad, Beef Carpacio, Salmon Steak and sea food pasta. First of all, they take so much time to even get the starters. Service is okay, too hyped for the quality. But most importantly that me and partner got extreme food poisoning!! We assume this was because on Thursday June 29th, Dahab got a full electricity outage for almost 48 hours, which means that most of the restaurants didn't have backup to keep their food storage working properly for almost 48 hours! It's quite sad that management of a place like this do not care about their customers health and well being. Instead of throwing everything away since almost everything got defrosted during the outage, they decided not to do so. In all honesty, the food didn't taste fresh at all. The Dai Pescatori Salad tasted really weird, shrimps were not fresh. The salmon steak didn't taste fresh, lacked seasoning. The sea food pasta was under cooked, we had to ask them to take it away. The calamari and shrimps in the pasta tasted extremely not fresh either. The only delicious thing was the apple pie with ice cream. It's also extremely over priced for the quality and service they offer. We go to way way better places that are fine dining in Cairo and pay the same amount, even less. Not recommended. 

Also, the waiters are wearing flip flops, which I find very weird and not hygienic by any means.

reviews.text: My friends and I recently visited The Caves in Dahab, a place we had heard so much about and were excited to explore. Any attempts to seek assistance or information were met with indifference, making us feel unwelcome from the start.The situation escalated when we were unexpectedly asked to leave the premises. This request came without any reasonable explanation and was delivered in a particularly rude manner. Our group was left feeling disheartened and upset, as we had been eagerly looking forward to this visit.The Caves themselves are undeniably beautiful, but the poor treatment we received completely overshadowed our experience. The staff's unprofessional and unfriendly behavior made what should have been a delightful visit into a very disappointing one.I sincerely hope that the management of The Caves takes immediate steps to address these issues. reviews.title: RUN AWAY FROM THIS PLACE: horrible service & people
reviews.text: RUN AWAY FROM THIS PLACE: horrible service & people. As you walk on the concourse everyone says come here. The Rep from this restaurant said come in. Our Taxi cab driver said, I am just the driver my Clients will decide. The Rep said if you have them come in your lunch will be free.  So we thought we we take him up on his offer. We sat, waited, 15 minutes later no one came to even give us menus. I didn't like the feeling in the place, it was just "off".  10 min later than came and got out order. However, 5 min later the same Rep pulled our taxi cab driver and told him "you brought in only 2 people, we won't give you anything".  My husband was furious, that he lied to us. It wasn't the amount of $, it was the principle: he lied. And my husband being an Egyptian, being treated by one like that, he got up and had us leave. At that point the Rep became very upset and raised his voice to my husband getting very upset/mad with him that we cancelled the order, not addressing how he lied to us.  Is this how you treat people. Like I said RUN AWAY FROM THIS PLACE!

reviews.text: This place has such a nice vibe. And it’s great that the owner is passing on such a warm and sweet work ethic to his sons. He buys Fresh what he expects he needs for each day; then closes when he runs out. His burgers are a testament of love, truly, for his business, his love of food, and his family. His prices are good, too. Also, the Drink with Me shop is next door, so that’s cool 😎. Enjoy! Oh, no fries though - but you can order a basket from KarKour, cheap and fresh.

reviews.title: The best burger in Dahab
reviews.text:
The place is very brightly painted, cosy, Khaled the owner is a SUPER friendly person with a welcoming smile always.
The burger is the best I have ever tasted in my life no kidding. Fresh, clean, juicy & very meticulously prepared. The bread is a special one.
His ingredients are always fresh so he finishes relatively early & you r lucky if you could catch him before he runs out coz once he is out of ingredients, he closes even if before his normal closing hour (10 pm) which is relatively early here in Dahab!
So if you r in for some juicy homemade clean burger, hit it FIRST right after the beach (after 4 pm) then go shower & enjoy the rest of the night!

reviews.title: Juicy nice burgers

The restaurant as a compliment provides 5-6 types of local sauces (tahini, baba Ganoush, chickpea paste, zajiki, garlic sour cream...) and airy hot tortillas, salads, fruit.

There were two shrimp in my seafood pasta 😂 and some fish stuff. And the price is 100 euros more expensive for the same dish than in neighboring restaurants. I hope this review helps you.

reviews.title: Optimal.

It's always a pleasure during your trip to Dahab to stop for lunch on the beautiful terrace of this place.
I always eat fish and find it excellent but my friends' chicken also smelled good. All served with rice, chips and delicious grilled vegetables.
The sauces and bread served while still warm are delicious.
I recommend to everyone

reviews.title: Poor quality, high Price
reviews.text:
I cannot recommend the restaurant;
We had as a starter:
- Lentil soup, which was good but compared to other Restaurants overpriced
- Baba ganoush plus tahine with pita: the pita was very dry, Baba ganoush tasteless; except the tahine was fabulous!

Main Menu:
- 600g Tomahawk steak, medium rare; it was medium rare but the quality of the Mega was very poor as the meat was very hard to chew. Mashed potatoes were good but rice was completely cold
- chicken kebab; i received a half chicken, cut in slices. Unfortunately all the bones were in and a lot of the meat was totally burned on the bottom side :( fries and rice were completely cold

The service was quick; overall bill was 1700(incl 1 coke and 1 sprite); the restaurant is big but not cozy and very loud.
We wont come back and prefer Shark or Friends Restaurant.

reviews.title: Poor service, very expansive, don't come near
reviews.text:
We waited for our dishes to come for more  than an hour.
When finally got them discovered that most of them were too small in content. 
When we got the bill we discovered that they added 14% tax (which wasn’t mentioned anywhere! and wasn’t charged from us in any other restaurant) to prices which initially appeared extremely high.
Talking to the owner about it we felt like literally dealing with Alcapone himself.
We ended up disappointed, hungry and with a feeling of being cheated.
Our strong advice - look for better value for money experience somewhere else.

reviews.title: Authentic Italian in Egypt
reviews.text:
This restaurant represents the crossroads of hospitality and Italian cuisine in Egypt. 

Mom's lasagna eat your heart out, is what I should have titled this review, but that would not pay enough respect to the mouth watering fresh flat bread pizzas. So instead, do yourself the favor and check-out this culinary gem for yourself. 

Ciao Bella, from Dahab.

reviews.title: Super recommended
reviews.text: Food delicious pizza spectacular also the ingredients delicious soft meat etc etc. congratulations continue so 😊

reviews.title: Feeling at home in Egypt
reviews.text:
A restaurant also equipped with 6 rooms where we found good food, hospitality and courtesy. Vincenzo, the owner, is Apulian and offers revisited Italian cuisine, in a wonderful combination with Egyptian tradition. The fresh pasta (noodles and ravioli) is homemade as is the tiramisu that Vincenzo personally prepares from the ladyfingers to mascarpone.
Excellent value for money 
Highly recommended!!!!

reviews.title: Our favourite restaurant
reviews.text: This is our favourite restaurant. Delicious food and beautiful beach setting. The farinata tastes amazing and the ravioli is so cheesy.  The steak is the best in town and well seasoned. Great place to eat when visiting Dahab.

reviews.title: Im not Gordon Ramsay but the food is average and needs new management
reviews.text:
The interior is lovely, the food was below average considering it’s an “authentic” Italian restaurant and the service was very poor and clearly badly managed. 
One starter came with our mains and the other came after we had finished eating, while the drinks were served after I had to physically go up to the bar as none of the 4 staff members were giving us any attention.
 Meanwhile, another table with “foreigners” were served extremely attentively and I felt i wasn’t valued seeing this through my experience. 
More stories to be told but to sum it up, this experience was quite disappointing and overpriced for the service you get.

reviews.title: Must eat there

Really good Italian food with very nice presentations.
We totally enjoyed our food and good service.
This did not look or give the feeling of a tourists trap joint, on the contrary!
Prices are very reasonable, especially when one considers the Egyptian Pound’s drop in price!
I highly recommend this place.
Enjoy.

reviews.title: Best pizza 🍕 in Dahab 😉
reviews.text:
Excellent cuisine, the best pizza in Dahab. The cocktail 🍸(guava, basil and coconut milk) is delicious.
Pizza with Gorgonzola cheese and herbs - delicious.
Breakfast omelet is wonderful with herbs and cheese and champignons - also delicious...

reviews.title: Authentic, simple and very friendly
reviews.text: Fabulous food…pizza is amazing. Owned by Vincenzo who is lovely and has the best handshake in town! Him and his staff are brilliant and couldn’t be more helpful. We stayed here as well as ate here. Rooms are simple, but clean and comfortable. Hop, skip and jump to the beach which they keep clean and serve drinks while you lounge. Very cute resident cats. Loved our stay here.

reviews.title: Best pizza I’ve ever had
reviews.text: Lovely location by the sea, with a beautiful and classy interior. Staff were very polite and chilled. This was the best pizza that I’ve ever had, shared their version of a “Four Seasons” and a great veggie one. The dough was fresh and rustic, generous toppings that were obviously of great quality. Was a great price 1200 EGP (approx. £30) for 2 pizzas a pasta and drinks and dessert. Overall a brilliant orchestrated restaurant with food that you’ll remember

reviews.title: Highly recommended
reviews.text: Very good service, high quality food + drinks for a reasonable pricing.. they didn’t lie when they said that their products are always fresh! Aside from the food and the drinks, the atmosphere of the place is very nice and relaxing.

reviews.title: Very bad experience at the restaurant
reviews.text: We went to the place  the two of us  on our usual good expectations of the pizza what happened is that we asked the waiter Kareem to try the steak if it's fresh and taste good he immediately recommended the rip eye and strangely short rips (it wasn't on the menu) then we wondered if we gonna add pizza to the two steaks gonna be too much he said no its totally fine and didn't mention that the rip eye is huge can easily be shared by three persons plus the rip eye we told him we want it medium it came out raw no even rare RAW so we send it back and still taste awful as for the rip eye it tasted horrible and stale the pizza was fine except he put such a huge pile of arugula over it ...over all it was extremely pricey and not recommended at all

reviews.title: Consistent High Quality

reviews.title: Gluten free options were great!!

reviews.text: Had wonderful last minute meal arrenged buy my best frind who recommend the restaurant to me the fish I had was absolutely delicious moist had nice sauce on top fresh tomatoes peppers beatufull spicy just right for me also we had prawns and calamari the food did come with sort difrent complement said dishes the service was straight forward nothing fancey the food did took abit of time I expected that as the fish fresh (I did pick it my self 👌) so prepare the fish and cook it do take time I am chef my self and understand that but it definitely worth the waite price wise it reasonable price, I would definitely go back and thank you sea bride for making my last meal very momerbel.. 🙏

reviews.title: Very disappointing
reviews.text: Used too dine here years ago and was good then, but not anymore. No communication with waiters, who can only say 'sorry', but speak nor understand English. Had to wait 45' for my fish to be served and another 15' for the soup, which seems only to be included for Egyptian customers now but not for foreigners (checking out, I was charged 5 EUR extra). By the time the soup arrived, the fish was cold. The soup was tasteless and the squid in it was like rubber. 'Grilled' fish was dry, not fresh. Pricing is not transparent: they weigh the fish of your choice in your presence, but don't tell you they'll charge you 14,55 EUR/kg for the cheapest fish to prepare it, which is more than the double compared to the price on the so-called 'menu'. For me, it came to a total of 12 EUR, mineral water included, which is far too much for Dahab standards; I refused to pay an extra 10% for the so-called 'service'. Do NOT recommend anymore.

reviews.title: Best choice for the lovers of sea food

reviews.title: Excellent seafood soup
reviews.text:
Gotta try the seafood soup. White not red. Haven't tried the red but the white is delish😋 and the calamari in it is so tender❣️never had it like that. Lightly battered Fried shrimp is also awesome. Cooking butterfly cut eating with hands with friends makes an enjoyable shared meal. They also serve fresh juices. Comes with pita and tahini.  white is delish😋 and the calamari in it is so tender❣️never had it like that. Lightly battered Fried shrimp is also awesome. 

Fish was ok. So were the grilled prawns. I recommend butterfly cut fish and eating with hands among friends (with good hygiene) makes an enjoyable shared experience. They also serve good fresh juices. Just tell them no sugar like everywhere else. Comes with pita and tahini.

After you order you choose whether you want it fried, or cooked on fire. Then you go to your table.
The seafood was really fresh and tasty, well made, and we really enjoyed it.
The salads were basic and ok.
I'd recommend this place.

reviews.title: Expensive

reviews.title: EWWWW realy terrible time spent there
reviews.text:
I had an absolutely terrible experience at Jackie's in Dahab, and I feel compelled to warn others before they waste their time.

During a salsa social, I was dancing and performed a lift with my partner—something that is completely normal and common in salsa dancing. Anyone who has ever attended a salsa social or has even basic knowledge of Latin dance knows that lifts are a natural part of the dance.

Out of nowhere, one of the staff members rushed over and approached me in an incredibly rude and aggressive manner. There was no polite conversation, no respectful request—just pure hostility. He spoke to me as if I had committed some kind of crime, when all I was doing was dancing. The level of disrespect was shocking and completely unacceptable.

To make matters worse, I was kicked out of the venue. Kicked out—for dancing at a dance event. Let that sink in.

The staff clearly has zero understanding of salsa culture. Salsa socials are meant to be spaces of joy, expression, freedom, and connection. Lifts, dips, and dynamic moves are part of what makes social dancing exciting. If your staff doesn't understand the very activity you're hosting, maybe you shouldn't be hosting it.

The way I was treated felt personal, discriminatory, and completely uncalled for. No paying guest should ever be humiliated and thrown out for simply enjoying a dance.

The only saving grace is that Jackie herself seems like a kind and well-meaning person. But unfortunately, her staff is single-handedly destroying the reputation of this place with their ignorance, rudeness, and power-tripping behavior.

If you're looking for a welcoming, respectful, and authentic salsa social experience—look elsewhere. This place is the exact opposite of what the Latin dance community stands for.

reviews.title: Terrible experience.. :(
reviews.text:
I had a really disappointing experience at Jackie’s in Dahab. What should have been a fun salsa social turned into something frustrating and uncomfortable.

While I was dancing with a girl who clearly didn’t mind, the staff stepped in and told me I wasn’t allowed to exchange contact information with her. That felt completely unnecessary and intrusive, especially in a social dance setting where meeting people is part of the whole point.

What made things worse is that it didn’t feel like everyone was being treated equally. It honestly seemed like they pick and choose who gets to enjoy themselves based on things like race, appearance, or even names. That kind of behavior has no place anywhere—especially not in a space that’s supposed to be about music, connection, and inclusivity.

Also, they don’t seem to understand the basics of Latin dance culture. Salsa socials are meant to be open, friendly, and welcoming—not restrictive or controlled like this.

The only positive thing I can say is that the owner, Jackie, seems like a genuinely nice person. Unfortunately, the staff and management completely ruin the experience.

Overall, I would not recommend this place if you’re looking for a real, enjoyable, and respectful social dance environment.

reviews.text:
12/12/23 - Tuesday late breakfast

We three middle aged guys from London were after a breakfast on the beach. The weather was quite windy but the sun was out and we made our way to the beach via the local town centre to the north to find the long empty beach scene (that may have been what the busy bit looked like 30 years ago) with sporadic private beaches. We made our way south towards the restaurant we had liked and dined at the day's late lunch before (EGV). 

At 11:05 we found this smart, quiet and spacious restaurant complex a few plots short of EGV. The menu was priced a bit less cheap than EGV for breakfast but substantially cheaper than anything in the busy area. We took a chance and found a table under the palm parasol. A youngish waiter brought us some menus. The table turned out to be in the strong wind and in the shade (so the wind chill factor was high without the heat of the sun compensating) so we moved to a larger table in the sun (but more wind) in front of the enclosed restaurant with big windows. 

There was no music thankfully, only the sound of the waves and wind so it was very relaxing. The proper seats were very comfortable too!

We chose our selection of two 'English' (150) and one Egg Shaskshouka (140) a double Turkish coffee (50) and a large bottle of still water (40). The waiter took his time returning for our orders, we almost gave up, but this place is so laid back.

We ordered and he took the menus away.

After a while the coffee arrived, after that eventually the bottle of water arrived with chilled glasses (nice touch) and we relaxed further. Odd that the water was not brought along with the Turkish coffee as it would be in any other place and does not need preparing.

After a fair wait the actual breakfasts arrived at 11:47. This place is laid back!! Even as it was nearly empty and we were the only people eating goodness knows how long things would take if busy. No problem though as we were not in a hurry.

The breakfasts were well presented on large plates. A fried egg, small bowl of baked beans, very nice mixed seed toasted bread, a packet of butter, sliced fried tomato, raw sliced tomato and cucumber. The two beef sausages were obviously not pork but were very pink, mushy inside (crisp outside) and fatty, so probably not much actual meat in them. In general it was quite good so no complaints. 

The Shaskshouka was a fried onions, tomatoes in a scrambled egg (soo quite plain) and our friend liked it. His Turkish coffee was fine too but no Cardamom like the EGV.

We ate the meal in the peace, sun and wind. The usual dog passed by and a cat turned up to beg. 

After the meal the waiter was quick to remove the plates but did not pressure us to leave as other people just sat around and read. 

My friends had a dip in the water but found the water too choppy and and the wind chill factor high on leaving.

On initially arriving I popped into the toilets across the road in the main complex which was quite smart and spacious. The toilets were clean and tidy. It looks like it gets popular in high season even though it is almost at the extreme northern end beyond the busy commercial 'beach'.

We spent another half hour sunbathing on their comfortable sunloungers and I did a quick litter pick on their beach in return (although the waiter had picked up some obvious litter earlier). I put the recovered ubiquitous plastic and cigarette butts in their non-recyclables bin by the till. We watched a sail surfer show off his flying skills which was quite entertaining.

Once again a small blond boy offered to sell his homework to us. Earlier some small girls tried to sell cotton bracelets to us. This seems to happen everywhere along the beach and the owners don't try to stop them. I imagine the families have be escaped their respective countries in the far north and are trying to make ends meet.

We left the beach happy and offered to pay the bill which came lower than expected. I challenged it and the waiter went through it again. It turned out the waiter had not added the 14% tax, probably because I helped him litter pick. We left a tip of 60 to round the bill up to 600 which was good value given the food and facilities. The coffee and desserts were cheaper than the EGV. One Egyptian dessert needed 30 minutes to prepare (which may have been ordered by one reviewer who did not notice the note). This place really is laid back! Do not come if you are in a hurry to go somewhere else!

reviews.text:
14/12/23 Thursday evening dinner

We three middle aged guys from London wanted our last evening meal in Egypt to be special. My two friends had been to this restaurant in January and liked it as it was obviously different from the usual Egyptian fare and good value on the beach strip (although on the land side).

We arrived at about 20:30 and took the empty larger table outside, noone else was dining, only a man smoking on the single table the other side of the entrance. No one was inside. 

A young, cheerful and friendly man greeted us and presented us with menus, a tray of hot hand towels and then a tray of three free 'apetisers' - dry rice in sweet and sour sauce - which was welcome.

We chose a variety of dishes, as we were close to the sea I went a bit overboard with the seafood dishes.

I ordered a seafood salad (155) and a mix seafood main (280) plus a steamed rice (30) but the waiter said that my main already had rice included. 
My friend ordered a shrimp konafa (but they had sold out) so he ordered a Pad Thai Koonge (215) instead and a mixed vegetables (100). 

Our friend chose a vegetable green curry (150) and a steamed rice, once again he was told the rice was included. We all ordered ours hot spicy as we are from London.

For drinks we ordered a large still water (at a very reasonable 20). The waiter left to pass the order to the kitchen staff. 

I needed to pop to the loo to wash my hands as I had been recycling some of our used bottles and cans in the only recycling bins in town (by the bridge nearby). I caught the waiter on his return and he took me round the side towards the hotel to the back of the restaurant where the toilet was up a few steps beside the kitchen door. I had also decided to order a pot of green tea too whilst being taken to the toilet entrance.

On returning I settled down to people watch. The water and tea came quickly with three tiny tea bowls which was nice. It was piping hot of course and was finished quite quickly whereupon I asked the waiter to top it up with more hot water which he duly did.

By 20:48 a tray of extras arrived, sliced red chilli, soy sauce and a spicy fish paste.

The dishes arrived at random it seemed, our friend's vegetables green curry first at 21:01, with a well sized bowl of rice. Our friend found it delicious and lapped it up!

The waiter then delivered my seafood salad at 21:02 and it was mixed clams, king prawns and squid (no fish, fair enough) in a spicy sauce. It certainly was different from what we had been eating most of the week and was a welcome change. The king prawns had been marinated well and were very tasty. The clams were mostly empty though which was a bit of a disappointment. There were plenty of prawns and squid though which I shared with my friends as we tend to share dishes anyway. In the middle of the salad was a finely sculpted hot red chili pepper garnish which I managed to eat, avoiding the seeds. It was all very tasty with a lot of coriander.

Within minutes at 21:06 my mixed seafood main arrived, I was hardly into my starter salad so the main got colder. It was also the same mix as the salad except hot with braised vegetables too. It was also generous with the seafood though and was very tasty again. The garnish was a sculpted pepper again on a bed of crispy thin noodles. I allowed more seafood to share around as I technically had ordered the most expensive options. The fish paste was a bit too weird for me with lots of umami flavour. The sliced chillies were the same as my raw chillies. The soy sauce was tasty as usual.  

I was eating both my starter and main when at 21:09 my friend's Pad Thai Koonge finally arrived with a bowl of rice for my main and another one for the Pad Thai which the waiter said we'd ordered (somehow) but he was happy to take it back as it was too much. We agreed, hoping it would not be included on the bill. The waiter also explained they had not made the Pad Thai hot so he left a bowl of chili powder. This is not quite the same as embedded spicy heat. The Pad ThaiThai was fine though as it was. 

My friend really liked his Pad Thai and at 21:14 his mixed vegetables arrived which were shared and delicious.

At some point a Thai woman arrived and ordered a takeaway, waiting at the order outside table. This was a good sign.

The service and food was brilliant. The waiter came over a couple of times to ask how we were and if we were happy, yes we were!

However.... 

Opposite us was a 
beach restaurant called Jackie's which seemed to be opening up with a loud techno party starting with Amy Winehouse's same (techno adaptation) song twice with a quiet gap in the middle and various loudspeaker buzzes and crackles. Another (albeit Egyptian) techno artist blasted away. It was not very pleasant and we could not hear each other talk at times. It bodes ill for the future of Dahab if they try to compete with resorts like Puerta Vallarta, Falliraki, Albufera or Playa del Rocha so driving down to the lowest common denominator. This can't be helped by Pattaya but they have to suffer it. Jackie's seems to be the only noisy place in town!! 

Furthermore:

As soon as the food started arriving we were surrounded by up to five very annoying cats who were begging, including scratching at trousers, sitting on the spare seat and trying to climb onto the table, jumping behind our backs onto our chairs, standing on the neighbouring shop's tables right behind us; all of this was very unnerving as we expected to be pounded upon and food stolen! The waiter had a go at chasing them away to no avail as they returned en masse very quickly.

And finally;

Quite often there were stray and pet dogs barking and facing each other off in the street. None of these could be prevented by the Pattaya owners but it meant our final evening meal was not perfect being marred by the three issues. I cannot knock any points off though.

Thankfully there were no beggars, hasslers, small girls selling fabric bracelets or small blond boys selling their paintings. Life is tough out there with high inflation and no pensions.

We finished by 21:50 not having any dessert as the techno and dog noise and cats' pestering was too much. We ordered the bill for our most expensive meal in the week we were in Egypt. 

The printed bill arrived at 21:55 and came in at 1058.40 which included 12% service charge in small print (lucky I saw that detail as we nearly left 1000 cash tip).

I paid by contactless debit card at Egyptian Pound rates. We left sated but a bit disappointed at our final meal.

The next day we did not have a proper lunch as we had to pack, checkout, coach back to Sharm, wander Neama Town and get to the airport for an evening flight. Our last proper meal was memorable for the wrong reasons. I hope other diners have better experiences in this excellent restaurant.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
The main reason I’m giving this place such a terrible review is the behaviour of the cashier when it came to the bill.

He added a 15% tip without asking me and, even worse, told me verbally what I supposedly owed without even showing me the bill. I had to ask to see the actual bill myself.

I had already waited approximately 25 minutes just to receive a bottle of water, so the idea that a tip was automatically added was ridiculous. I was actually prepared to leave a tip voluntarily, but after this experience I felt completely different.

What makes it even more uncomfortable is that I’m not a local, and I genuinely got the impression that this 15% was being added because I was a foreign customer. I cannot know for certain whether that was the reason, but the way it was handled certainly made me suspicious.

This is not how tipping works. A tip is supposed to be voluntary. You do not simply decide what the customer should pay, add 15%, and tell them the total without even presenting the bill.

I honestly wonder whether the owner/management is even aware that this is happening. If this is something the cashier is doing on his own, management should seriously investigate it.

I would strongly recommend that anyone eating here checks the bill carefully before paying, particularly tourists and other foreign visitors. What happened to me left me feeling that I had been deliberately pressured into paying extra.

The worst part is that I would have happily left a tip if the service had been good and I had been given the choice. Instead, the way it was handled made me feel taken advantage of and extorted.

Check your bill. Don’t assume the amount you are verbally told is the actual amount you should be paying.

reviews.title: Highly variable experience but delicious
reviews.text:
I want to be as supportive as possible of places like The Vegan Lab, that provide vegan and gluten-free options in places where this is rare. My first visit was excellent - the time from order to receiving my food (the 'seaside toast') was over 30 mins but it was a generous portion, the GF bread was thickly sliced and delicious, as was the hummus, and the plate was full of lovely, pea-sized cherry tomatoes bursting with flavour, as well as cucumber, fresh herbs and olives. The next time I went, the server didn't seem to understand my query as to whether another dish could be made GF, so I defaulted to the seaside toast again. I got three small, thin slices of clearly defrosted bread, soft in the middle but very hard at the edges. Each slice of bread came with 2 slices of cucumber, and 2-3 cherry tomatoes. It was like eating a starter rather thanthe main course I had previously. I also twice had a decaf single espresso, and was charged considerably more the second time (2 days later), "because it's decaf". Meanwhile, the woman sitting across from me was given something different from what she ordered.
Lovely decor, staff try their best but don't seem familiar with what's on the menu, and the lack of consistency in dish quality, portion size and prices is frustrating or at least means you don't know what you're going to get. 
They also offer the option of ordering, 1 day in advance, some of their food - hummus, GF bread, coconut yoghurt, tempeh etc - to take home, which is a great idea. They're a little on the expensive side for Egypt prices but it was nice to buy some hummus and use it for my meals at home.

They probably just wanted to get rid of all the leftovers of the day, taking the advantage that I was not going to it in front of them and that I couldn't complain... reviews.title: Overengineered food

The burger componets tasted bland and overprocessed, with a remarkably uniform consitency for the 'cheese', the patty and the bun. Vegan, but definitely neither tasty nor healthy. Can't speak for the rest of the menu here.
I wish the restaurant would focus on more simple vegan cuisine, instead of mimicing meat and dairy products and using fancy (overprocessed) ingredients. I'll stick to home-made vegan meals here.

reviews.title: Amazing Moroccan food cooked with love.
reviews.text:
It is rare to find somewhere that does fantastic food with love for the cuisine on offer. Bab el-Bahr Grand Maghreb is one of these precious pearls in a sea of burger and pizza places that have flooded Dahab.

I found it whilst looking for somewhere totally different to eat and having recently been to Agadir, I was attracted to this restaurant by the rave reviews and the promise of a good tagine.

And boy did it deliver. From the lovely welcome at the Hotel Monica reception who quickly guided me up the ten or so shallow steps it took to get to the restaurant to the warm greeting by the two lovely women who run this place (I feel mortified I never introduced myself or asked their names!)

I told the lady who was in charge of service that I was happy for her to choose for me between beef or chicken tagine. I opted for the potatoes and olives version. 

It did take a while (about 20 minutes or so) for the food to arrive but that is because it is all made fresh to order for the guest. So please don’t go there and complain about delays but the wonderful smells coming from the kitchen will definitely whet your appetite while you wait.

The beef tagine was served accompanied by the fluffiest melt in the mouth couscous that 
 I have ever had, the beef was tender and flavoursome and the fresh tomato salad was a perfect accompaniment. Each mouthful was better than the previous. I felt almost bereft when the meal was over. The complimentary green tea with mint refreshed the palate and was a perfect ending to a perfect meal.

Finding the restaurant was super easy, it is just a few minutes away from the central area in Mashraba in a quiet but brightly lit street, away from the hussle and bustle just a few metres away. Don’t hesitate to go and savour the magnificent tagines!

Everything was delicious. Warm pita bread, seemed like fresh made, probably the best hummus we had in almost a month now in Egypt and the mossaka was not what we expected but was delicious. We rarely repeat restaurants specially on a place with so many options but here we went back for the great food and extremely friendly service.

We were made to feel like royalty.  The team were friendly not pushy, attentive but not intrusive and they catered for our every need wether it was making sure the cats didn't come to our table, or making menu alterations to suit our requests. The partners in this business know their stuff and they employ people who know their stuff also and as a team, they are superb!  A firm favourite...they even made us a pack up for the trip home!!!  I cannot wait to return and see our new friends at Sea Houses be it for Breakfast, lunch or dinner.  We also visited as a couple but will without doubt be returning as a family

reviews.title: great restaurant with great staff!
reviews.text:
We stayed in Dahab for 8 nights and we had 4 formal dinner at Sea House, that shows how much we love this place! 
The location is great right on the water, easy to find. It also has a seafood display on ice so you can order whatever you desire for. We always hand pick the fish for our dinner. The set meal is a superb value...we got three course meal for a set price depending on the size of fish or type of seafood. The first course is excellent with fresh baked Egyptian bread, 6 kinds of dipping sauce, Turkish tea. The main course is a big plate of seafood (grilled or fried fish) with grilled fresh veggies, and the desert is chef's choice so you will be surprise everytime!
The host and staff are friendly with warm heart. We negotiate the set menu depending on the size of fish and always get great price with great service. It is sad to say goodbye to the staff and Sea House.
Highly recommend the Sea House Restaurant if you ever visit addictive Dahab!

reviews.title: Unsafe experience
reviews.text:

We ate our two meals, appetizer and deserts (all of which were really awful and totally beneath the standards of other Dahab restaurants). We were then told we owed 1850 LE cash. Clearly we were being very overcharged for the meals and also paying for the "free" items. This was a small amount of money to us so we didn't mind paying it, but we of course were not carrying that much cash around. So the waiter followed us closely and stood closely beside us in a threatening manner when we went to two ATM machines to get his money. Most of the money certainly went into his pocket and not to the restaurant. 

I've lived in Dahab before, have visited many times since and have eaten at a wide variety of restaurants throughout the years and never had anything remotely like this happen before. If this happens to you, you can go to the police station right across the street from Kwanza and report them to the police.

The starters (inexplicably brought at the same time as the main course) were warm Egyptian bread, and little dishes of salad, tahini, and baba ganouch — which is complementary in all the Dahab restaurants.

reviews.text:
11/12/23 Monday evening snack

We three middle-aged guys were staying locally for a few days. We had had a lunch on the beach and by late evening wanted a snack. My friends had been here in January and liked the food, especially the felafel. I looked it up on TA (not entered) and GglMps to find mixed reviews, some believable, others obviously not.

We arrived at about 19:50 to find a European woman and her son eating and two groups of local men on other tables eating out of stoneware bowls. We secured a spare table by the road and two of us went to the counter to choose. There were no felafel on display, only various cooked vegetables, sauces and a shredded salad. 

The young man was filling a bread up with a mix of these and put them on a plate. Another was asking what we wanted but we were not sure as there were no prices anywhere and we are vegetarians (some of the dishes looked like they had chicken in). After a certain amount of confusion I just said 'same as that' pointing at the finished filed bread, not knowing what it might cost. He said 'mix' and I agreed. He then offered a polystyrene tray or black plastic small bowl. We were sitting so he should have realised eat in was our preference. No matter I chose the tray (although yet more plastic to be disposed of since COP27 nearby). 

He skirted round the trays with a spoon and filled the tray with the stuffed bread, a few crisps, a large spoonful of chips and two felafel. I asked 'how much?'and he then asked an older guy (at the cashier table in the middle) 'how much?' in Egyptian. There was a lot of confusion and I got my money out (small denominations!) at his table and he said '40' quietly but I did not here if it was '14' or '40'. He then wrote down '40'. That was only £1 so I thought it was fine considering the size and variety. He was happy! Maybe I did pay over the odds but it was still viral for us although we were cash cows for them.

I showed my 'dish' to my friends and they agreed to have another one each so I asked the young man for two more then went to the old man and paid him 120. A few minutes later a similar tray with two stuffed breads was ready, not quite the same as the first as no chips or felafel at the side and definitely smaller overall so there was interesting portion control. He also used his fingers at times, no blue nitrile gloves here! 

I returned to the table with the second tray and my friends wanted a spicy sauce (none was provided on the table). Back to the counter I went and more confusion (as the boss got involved too) as there were no sauces but there was cayenne/chilli powder ina large tray which the young man put a spoon full of it into another polystyrene tray with two plastic spoons. Oh well, do much for the 'Make Dahab Plastic Free' murals on some walls nearby. 

I returned and eventually managed to start eating my (now going cold) stuffed bread and 'garnish'. My friends had theirs. 

They were actually delicious! A bit of chili helped but do not breathe in! There was no meat in them at all thankfully, just braised tasty vegetables and the mix of 'dips' and salad. The chips and crisps were a bit soggy though.

Mine was the biggest as I said and my friends said their felafel and chips were inside although still ultimately smaller. It was a messy eat though and I had to use the plastic spoons to finish my filling snack. There were no napkins or washing facilities available so my fingers were smelly at the end so bring your own tissues. There were also no drinks available either so maybe it is BYO (non alcoholic obviously).

During our stay other locals and westerners popped in to eat, this was popular!

We left sated and happy around 20:30 to do some 'Drinkies' shopping opposite and buy a waiter's friend. The snack has just hit the spot and was not a rip-off as some (dubious) reviews had mooted.

reviews.title: Delicious, but Foreigners Beware
reviews.text:
Very popular in the morning with food being turned over quick. The falafel and fries were great and fresh. The fries were unique with a thick batter and excellent seasoning. I'd recommend it, but it's staffed by hustlers that scam foreigners.

This place has an interesting way of working. There's no menu or visible prices. You're suppose to tell the staff at the small table what you want, you ask prices, negotiate, and pay. You're then given a ticket that you give to the counter. This is what locals do, but foreigners are seated or told to order at the counter then eat. The problem is if you eat before paying, you forfeit your right to a fair value. Two plain falafel sandwiches and a small plate of fries should be 20 LE, but ended up costing 50 LE.

It's a delicious place to eat, but expect to pay triple the normal price.

The restaurant is located on the roof of a hotel near the lighthouse, with a great view of the whole bay.
The entrance to the restaurant is through the entrance to the hotel and you have to go up the stairs.
The design, the furniture and the entire restaurant area are tastefully decorated, look great and are also very comfortable to sit and eat.
The food itself is excellent, every dish we tried was accurately prepared and served at just the right moment, a wonderful combination of delicious food, a great atmosphere and a perfect view.
In addition to all this, I must mention the perfect service of the restaurant staff, and especially the manager Hissam and the owner Miro.
